newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock exchange dull at start of week.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock exchange dull at start of week.

text.p: Jordan's stock exchange started weekly trade on Saturday with buying minimal, dealers said.
Shares worth 337,178 dinars ($476,240) changed hands, up from 295,436 dinars on Wednesday, the last day of weekly trade.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell a marginal 0.04 points to 147.68 points, continuing a pattern of tight range trade since early October.
The exchange is blighted by high domestic interest rates and worries over barriers to trade with sanction-hit Iraq to the east and with Israel and the Palestinian territories to the west.
Blue-chip Arab Bank Group again accounted for nearly a third of the total turnover, worth nearly 118,080 dinars, with a 0.5 dinar drop to close at 246.00 dinars.

Aside from Middle East Investment Bank, the second busiest stock with 33,365 dinars worth of trade, there was hardly any dealing of significance, traders said. The bank's stock rose a marginal 0.01 dinar to 1.05 dinars.

Blue-chip Jordan Cement,, focus of foreign investor interest with government plans to sell a substantial portion of its shares in the company, remained unchanged at 3.30 dinars with 6,327 shares changing hands.
Overall, fifteen declined and nine advanced, while 13 traded but closed unchanged.
